summary: Bluff Park (Hoover) fire tower, 100 ft, built 1941 per the Star. Torn down in 1992; its restored cab stands in a small park on Patton Chapel Road.

facts.design: 100-foot steel Aermotor tower with a lookout cab; only the cab survives
facts.status_note: Tower torn down in 1992; only the top cab survives, restored and displayed in Hoover

access.note: Cab sits in a small park with a historic marker on Patton Chapel Road; drive-up. No hours or permit rules found in the sources read.

events.note: Anniston Star item of 1 May 1941 reports the new 100-foot tower and its dedication. The Hoover Sun's 63 years of service before 1992 point to about 1929.
National Geodetic Survey description still calls it an Alabama state fire lookout tower, about 100 ft
Tower torn down; cab removed and kept on city property
A Hoover Fire Department member found the cab on a lot at Fire Station No. 4; the restoration project began in May 2011
Restored cab dedicated 31 October. The year is inferred: the article says the project began in May 2011 and 'last year'. The cached text has no dateline.
Cab placed in a small park on Patton Chapel Road across from Hoover Fire Station No. 2. Year inferred, as above.

corrections.why: The tower was torn down in 1992 and only its cab survives. This record is very likely the same tower as us-al-crawford, which is already marked gone.
The register says the site is administered by the City of Hoover. The state ran the tower in 1941 and 1971 (see cites 1 and 2).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The May 1941 Star item gives the dedication year. The Hoover Sun's 63 years of service before 1992 point to about 1929. The story gives both and uses 1941 as the event year.

sources.title: Partnership leads to preservation of Bluff Park icon

notes_for_editor: Very likely the same tower as us-al-crawford (firetower.org record US 1614, AL 3, 'Crawford Lookout Site', status gone, coordinates 33.3862, -86.8291). This record's coordinates (33.3889, -86.8559) are about 2.5 km away. Recommend merging the two; not done here. The Hoover Historical Society page returned HTTP 403 and was not read; it may give current hours. The 2012 dedication year is inferred, not printed in the cached article. The 1941 date (Star) and the about-1929 date (Hoover Sun's 63 years) disagree, and the story says so.
